dict.string: While you hold the board button, Felt Notes listens so you can call the flop, turn and river aloud. Nothing is recorded or uploaded.
The board cards you call aloud are recognised on this iPhone and turned into cards. Nothing is uploaded.

Felt Notes (beta) can read your own two hole cards with the camera: from one photo you take, or, with Watch my cards on, from the live view while you peek. It also reads the organizer's table-night QR code from a photo. Those images are read on your phone, never saved and never uploaded. Only if you start Record the table does it save photos of the table, on this iPhone, for you to export yourself.
Optional: tags a table recording with roughly where it was made, so you can tell your recordings apart. It stays on this iPhone.

Felt Notes uses Bluetooth to find a home game hosted by a phone at your table, so you can join it with one tap without internet, and to measure how far apart the phones in that game are. It only looks for other phones running Felt Notes.
While you are in a home game, Felt Notes measures how far apart the iPhones in that game are, to test working out who sits where. It is only used during a game or while recording the table.
Felt Notes looks for a Chromecast on your Wi-Fi so it can show tonight's table on the TV. It only sends the table code, never your screen or your cards.
